deep.reconstruction:
Setting (from previous and next pages): X is a stratified space, or more generally a 'stratified topos' (e.g. a scheme with its étale topology). Y ⊂ X is a closed stratum and X* = X \ Y is the open complement. V_{Y,X} is the germ of a tubular neighbourhood of Y, homotopy equivalent to Y. V*_{Y,X} is the deleted tubular neighbourhood germ (the 'link bundle' of Y in X). Both germs are of 'infinitesimal' nature.

The previous page proposes reconstructing the homotopy type of X as the homotopy pushout of X* <- V*_{Y,X} -> V_{Y,X}. Truncating to 1-types gives a van Kampen statement: the square of fundamental groupoids (8) is cocartesian.

This page restates (8) in group language. Assume X, Y, X* are connected. Choose a base point of V*_{Y,X}; in the SGA1 spirit Grothendieck defines a base point as a universal covering of V*. This induces base points on V, X* and X, and gives a canonical isomorphism (9): π1(X) ≅ π1(X*) *_{π1(V*_{Y,X})} π1(V_{Y,X}). Here π1(V_{Y,X}) is 'exterieurement' isomorphic to π1(Y), i.e. isomorphic up to inner automorphism, since the identification V ≃ Y moves the base point.

To describe π1(X) from 'elementary' data π1(Y) and π1(X*), one must still describe π1(V*) and its two maps (diagram (10)): π1(V*) -> π1(Y) and π1(V*) -> π1(X*). A marginal note says the arrow to π1(Y) is only defined modulo the choice of a base point y in Y and a path from x to y, i.e. up to conjugation.

The page ends: 'this is where the hypothesis' of local triviality (normal equisingularity) enters. The next page turns this into a definition. It requires that V*_{Y,X} -> V_{Y,X} ≃ Y be a homotopy fibration whose fibre is the local link V*_{z,X} at a point z of Y. This 'homotopical local triviality' is proposed as the definition for étale stratified toposes, using profinite (or localized) homotopy types. That makes π1(V*) an extension of π1(Y) by a quotient of π1 of the local link, which makes (10) computable.
errors: The amalgamated-product form (9) silently requires V*_{Y,X} to be connected. Connectedness of X, Y and X* does not guarantee this: e.g. Y of real codimension 1 separating locally, or several local branches of X along Y. In general only the groupoid statement (8) is correct. The choice of a single base point of V* presupposes connectedness.

Minor: the identification π1(V) ≅ π1(Y) is only exterior (up to inner automorphism). Grothendieck notes this himself, so the 'canonical' isomorphism (9) is canonical only after the base-point/path choices he describes.

Validity of the homotopy-pushout/van Kampen statement requires tameness hypotheses (existence of good tubular neighbourhood germs, or a suitable hypercovering/excision in the topos setting). These are assumed, not proved here.

ideas.what: Van Kampen for a stratified space: X as homotopy pushout of complement X*, deleted neighbourhood V* and tubular neighbourhood V ≃ Y; π1(X) as amalgam π1(X*) *_{π1 V*} π1(Y)
ideas.modern_name: Seifert–van Kampen / homotopy pushout decomposition along the link (gluing via homotopy links)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Classical (van Kampen 1933, Brown for groupoids); in stratified form Quinn 1988, Hughes, Woolf; Lurie HA App. A
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme (1984), §§5-6 on tame topology and dévissage of stratified structures, discusses tubular neighbourhoods and links in a similar spirit; exact formula unsure

ideas.what: Base point defined as a universal covering (fibre functor viewpoint)
ideas.modern_name: Base point as fibre functor / universal pro-covering

ideas.what: Need to compute π1(V*) and its maps to π1(Y), π1(X*) as 'elementary data'; arrow defined only up to path choice (exterior homomorphism)
ideas.modern_name: Outer homomorphisms; link-bundle fundamental group as extension of π1(stratum) by π1(local link)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Standard; the extension structure follows from fibration of the holink (Quinn)

ideas.what: Lead-in to next page: local triviality of the stratification defined homotopically as V* -> V ≃ Y being a homotopy fibration with fibre the local link, in étale/profinite setting
ideas.modern_name: Homotopically stratified sets (Quinn's holink fibration condition); étale homotopy links / exodromy
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme hints at a dévissage theory for stratified structures; this precise definition not known to me in published texts

missed.claim: Together with the following page, Grothendieck proposes defining 'local triviality' of a stratification in a topos (e.g. étale topos of a scheme) purely homotopically. The condition is that the deleted-neighbourhood germ maps to the neighbourhood germ (≃ stratum) as a homotopy fibration with fibre the local link, using profinite types. This anticipates Quinn's homotopically stratified spaces (1988) and the étale homotopy links / exodromy programme of Barwick–Glasman–Haine. This page itself only sets up the van Kampen motivation.
missed.quote: Pour expliciter π1(X) en termes de données "élémentaires" ... il faudrait encore : expliciter la structure de π1(V*_{Y,X})
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Historical priority and motivation: it ties van Kampen-type computation of étale π1 of stratified schemes to a homotopical equisingularity condition. That condition is not standard in the étale literature as a definition.

deep.surprise_reason: The page itself is a routine van Kampen amalgam for a stratum, its tubular neighbourhood and its link. The interest lies in the context: an early homotopical/étale stratification programme anticipating Quinn and exodromy, which is partly visible in the Esquisse. Nothing on this page alone would surprise a specialist.
transcription_corrections: Line (9): the amalgam subscript is π1 V*_{Y,X} (with star), and the underbrace on π1(V_{Y,X}) reads '≃ π1(Y)'. The transcription is correct here.

The margin note to (10) is only partly legible. It appears to say the arrow is defined modulo inner automorphisms, depending on a base point of Y and a choice of path from x to y. The transcription 'défini mod. des chemins [?]' should be read with that sense.
In diagram (10) the target was first written π1(X) then corrected to π1(Y); the transcription '[-X-]Y' is right.
The struck line 'Calculatif : un pt base choisi de' is uncertain; the first word may differ.
